title: With what help will the bright one come to us?

words.context: Sāyaṇa on the Ṛgveda: «चित्रः चायनीयः पूजनीयः», ‘to be honoured’

words.role: with bhuvat: ‘come to, be present with’

words.meaning: will he be, will he come

words.context: Sāyaṇa: «मित्रभूत इन्द्रः», the friend is Indra

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a vowel other than a loses its visarga; the vowels stay apart
t before a vowel becomes d

morphology.note: Vedic instrumental singular in -ī for later ūtyā.
an aorist subjunctive of √bhū, with ā: ‘will he come to be with’.

translation.literal: With what help will the bright one come to us, the ever-growing friend? With what most powerful course?
translation.readable: With what help will he come to us, the bright one, our friend who is always growing — with what mighty power?

meaning: A question in praise: with what help, with what mighty power, will the bright one, our ever-growing friend, come to us? In the Ṛgveda (4.31.1) the friend is Indra, as Sāyaṇa says. In the Navagraha sūktam it is the first mantra for Rāhu, recited before āyaṃ gauḥ and yat te devī. The witness gives no reason for the choice, and none is offered here.
in_the_rite: Step 8 (Rāhu), first mantra. The use of a Vedic verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition; the commentary below speaks of the verse in its Vedic setting. In the Saṃhitā (TS 4.2.11) it is a puronuvākyā; Sāyaṇa’s viniyoga names the offering.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa’s viniyoga places the verse in the Saṃhitā as the invitatory verse (puronuvākyā) of an offering on one potsherd: «अथ कायमेककपालमित्यस्य पुरोनुवाक्यामाह».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: On the Ṛgveda verse Sāyaṇa takes the friend to be Indra: «सदावृधः सदा वर्धमानः चित्रः चायनीयः पूजनीयः सखा मित्रभूत इन्द्रः», and the question as «कया उती ऊत्या तर्पणेन नः अस्मान् आ भुवत् आभिमुख्येन भवेत्».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A gāyatrī of three eight-syllable pādas; the first two are printed as one line. The Taittirīya and the Ṛgveda (4.31.1) have the same words.
